summary.headline: Aditya Vision Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28.1% YoY to Rs 586.23 crore and PAT 45.2% to Rs 18.47 crore, with October demand described as slow.
summary.overview: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT all grew strongly in Q2 FY27, with H1 revenue up 27.3% to Rs 1,778.91 crore and same-store sales growth at 18%. Gross margin expanded 125 bps to 16.3%, but management attributed only about 75-80 bps of the quarter's margin gain to price hikes and guided normalised gross margin at 15-15.5%. Management said demand has been slow in October and expects a pick-up toward Dhanteras and Diwali. The store network reached 214, with new entries into Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal, and the company guided to about 230-235 stores by FY27 end.

segments.name: Bihar
segments.commentary: Contributed about 73% of Q2 revenue across all 38 districts, with 120 stores.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: Contributed about 15% of Q2 revenue from 56 stores across 32 of 75 districts.

segments.name: Jharkhand
segments.commentary: Contributed about 11% of Q2 revenue from 33 stores across 22 of 24 districts.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh
segments.commentary: Contributed about 1% of Q2 revenue from five stores across three of 33 districts; newly entered state.

guidance_outlook: Normalised gross margin guided at around 15%-15.5% at constant prices; price-driven gains are not built into guidance.
EBITDA margin guided at 8%-10% on an annual basis; management said margin will moderate as price-driven gross margin gains fade, with the impact that year roughly equal to the gross margin effect.
Store count expected at around 230, possibly up to 235, by end FY27, and about 35 more stores in FY28 (about 270 total).
Chhattisgarh: 9-10 more stores planned. Madhya Pradesh: about 3 stores shortly and 15-17 in the coming year. West Bengal: at least 15 stores, with 40-50 stores possible over about four years.
New-store breakeven expected in about one year; management said new-state margin dilution would be offset by maturing older stores.
capex_capacity: Capex per store is about Rs 90 lakh, up from earlier levels due to inflation over the last 1.5 years.
Capex in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh could be 10%-15% higher than in core markets due to freight and vendor logistics costs, depending on store size.
Retail footprint expanded 18.3% to about 9.51 lakh sq ft as of September 30, 2026.
Entered West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh in the period (as of October 2026); two West Bengal stores opened and two more in progress.
Cluster-based expansion leverages logistics, vendor relationships and brand recall.
demand_pricing: Management said demand has been slow in October and expects a pick-up as Dhanteras and Diwali approach.
Q2 growth was led by AC, followed by mobile and refrigerators, helped by an extended summer.
Around 75-80 bps of the Q2 gross margin gain came from OEM price increases; the rest came from normal trading.
H1 same-store sales growth was 18%, versus 2% in H1 FY26 when unseasonal rains hurt footfall.
West Bengal competitors include Reliance and Croma, plus a local chain, which are stronger in metros than in peripheral districts; the company is targeting border districts near Bihar first.
Headwinds cited: West Asia conflict, energy disruption, higher crude prices, Bihar floods and cyclone, and rising staples and cooking gas prices.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 125 bps gross margin expansion in Q2, and is the full-year margin guidance changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes contributed about 75-80 bps and normal trading the rest; normalised gross margin guidance stays at 15%-15.5% at constant prices.

qa_highlights.question: How has demand been in October and was the festive season delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales have been slow so far, but expects a pick-up toward Dhanteras and Diwali; it could not predict the outcome precisely.

qa_highlights.question: Why did indirect expenses rise sharply YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said OPEX was controlled and at a similar sales ratio. Higher indirect costs reflect financing, credit card, CMS and freight costs scaling with sales, plus about 30 stores added in the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and breakeven for new stores in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about Rs 90 lakh per store, with breakeven expected in about one year; management said it was too early to guide on the new states specifically.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 8th Pay Commission be a demand driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would be a strong tailwind through higher discretionary spending, but depends on the macro environment.

risks_watch: Slow October demand; whether the festive pick-up materialises before Dhanteras and Diwali.
Normalisation of gross margin after price-driven gains, which management said will moderate EBITDA margin in the same proportion.
Indirect expense growth (Rs 17 crore to about Rs 28 crore YoY in Q2 per analyst, +64%) as the company enters new states.
Breakeven and margin dilution in new states (Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal) and competition from national chains in West Bengal.
Inventory at Rs 865 crore (up from Rs 840 crore since March 2026) and borrowings of Rs 293 crore (up YoY from prior-year levels).
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year execution and the 8%-10% EBITDA margin range, but cautious and vague on near-term demand, saying sales are slow and hard to predict. Management was also evasive on quantifying the cyclone impact and new-state breakeven.

growth.why: Management guides ~230-235 stores by FY27 end (from 214) and ~35 more in FY28, with specific state-level store plans and ~Rs 90 lakh capex per store, but no revenue growth figure is guided, the October demand is slow, and ~75-80 bps of the Q2 margin gain came from price hikes that management says will fade.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin is guided to 15-15.5% against 16.3% in Q2 as price-led gains fade, and management said EBITDA margin will moderate by roughly the same amount, while new-state dilution is expected until breakeven in about one year.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Store count went from 214 to a guided ~230-235 by FY27 end (about 16-21 more stores), with two West Bengal stores opened and two in progress, and ~35 more stores planned in FY28 (~270 total).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 same-store sales grew 18% and revenue 27.3%, but October demand is slow and growth depends on a Dhanteras and Diwali pick-up, with store additions of about 7.5% (214 to ~230) supporting volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already set at about Rs 90 lakh per store and store plans for Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal are specified, so further store-level capex is committed; no utilisation figure was given, so no new capex programme is confirmed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no revenue growth guide, price-driven margin gains are excluded from guidance, and October demand is slow with festive pick-up only expected, not confirmed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: October demand was slow, and management guided normalised gross margin at 15-15.5% after 75-80 bps of Q2's 125 bps gain came from price hikes that will fade, though the 8-10% EBITDA margin guide was held.

rows.label: West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh entry scale-up
rows.why: West Bengal has at least 15 stores planned with 40-50 possible over about four years, and Madhya Pradesh has about 3 shortly plus 15-17 in the coming year, though new-state breakeven is about one year away.

rows.label: Inventory and borrowings rising
rows.why: Inventory rose to Rs 865 crore from Rs 840 crore since March 2026 and borrowings are at Rs 293 crore, up YoY, which could pressure cash flow as stores expand.

rows.label: Festive season demand pick-up
rows.why: Management said October sales were slow and expects a pick-up toward Dhanteras and Diwali, but could not predict the outcome precisely.

tone.note: Management was confident on store expansion and the 8-10% EBITDA margin guide but cautious on slow October demand and evasive on new-state breakeven and cyclone impact; analysts probed indirect expense growth and margin sustainability.
